title: Dynamic token reservation with hybrid overload dropper for Dedicated routing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a new admission control strategy for Dedicated fleets that combines lightweight token reservation (for throughput guarantees) with a hybrid overload dropper to preserve latency SLOs and fairness during transient spikes. This ticket covers the routing-layer changes, client-visible queue handles, metrics, rollout plan, and integration with autoscaler signals.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant throughput reservation tokens can be requested and consumed by the routing layer (reservation API annotated on existing route configs)
Under synthetic overload tests, p95 inference latency increase must be <= 25% for reserved classes and <= 2x for best-effort classes compared to baseline
System-level shedding rate is controllable by policy and observable in dashboards (shed_rate, reserved_blocked, queue_depth)
Canary rollout enabled behind feature flag and validated on two Dedicated customer fleets; rollback within 30 minutes if errors spike > 3x
Provide clear client backpressure contract: responses include X-Redwood-Queue-Handle for queued requests and 429 when immediate reject is applied

Rollout: feature flag, canary to 10% fleets, monitor dashboards and error budgets - Ops
notes: Motivation: several Dedicated customers reported tail latency spikes during cross-tenant bursts where best-effort traffic dominated shared queues. Reservation allows predictable throughput for critical tenants without over-provisioning fleet-wide.

High-level approach: allocate lightweight ephemeral tokens representing N rps or tokenized throughput per tenant/route. Router consumes tokens before dispatch. If tokens are exhausted, requests can be queued (with a bounded handle) or shed based on configured policy.

Hybrid dropper rationale: pure probabilistic dropping protects system capacity quickly but can be unfair. Combining probabilistic shedding with a per-client deficit tracker (tracks shortfalls vs reserved rate) preserves long-term fairness while allowing fast emergency shedding.

Client-visible queue handle: returns X-Redwood-Queue-Handle header when request is queued; clients may poll with handle to check status or cancel. This avoids long-lived HTTP connections causing head-of-line issues.

Autoscaler integration: reservation occupancy and queue_signal will feed into the Dedicated autoscaler to trigger scale-up earlier for persistent reservation pressure. Short spikes should be handled by shedder without scaling.
- Strong reservations reduce overall statistical multiplexing and may increase unit cost. We expose burst and sustained knobs to help customers trade cost vs guarantee.
- Queue handles add API complexity but provide better client UX than opaque 429s for transient waitable work.
- We opted for a hybrid dropper instead of strict priority preemption to avoid starvation of best-effort workloads during prolonged bursts.
Operational safety: feature-flag gated, default reservations off. Default cluster-level policy set to 'soft-shed' for best-effort tenants.
Related incidents: INC-2025-07-11-dedicated-tail-latency (linked in Confluence) motivated this work. Short postmortem highlighted poor isolation between employers using same fleet.
Security: token metadata contains only opaque reservation_id; no PII. KMS used for signing handles if persistence across control plane needed. Security review requested.

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (FF off): deploy routing and shedder code behind feature flags to staging and canary fleets
Phase 2 (10% canary): enable reservation for low-risk tenants; monitor reserved_token_utilization, p95/p99 latency, and shed_rate
Phase 3 (50%): open reservation to paid tenants with clear billing meter for reserved capacity
Phase 4 (GA): enable in UI/Console with billing and on-by-default per tenant if purchased
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: reservation fragmentation reduces efficient packing of requests. Mitigation: provide consolidation tool and recommend sustained vs burst sizing guidelines.
Risk: leaked queue handles leading to memory growth. Mitigation: TTL + periodic GC + metrics alert for handle retention > 1h.
Risk: incorrect shedder tuning may cause cascading retries. Mitigation: introduce jittered client backoff suggestions in docs and rate-limited retry headers.
Risk: autoscaler thrash if short spikes cause scale events. Mitigation: autoscaler requires sustained reservation occupancy > 2 minutes before scale-up unless overridden by admin policy.
